scope: Retrospective paired diagnostic of MP31 existing simulated records. MP31 and MP32 aggregate results were known before this protocol. No independent new biological or simulated observations are claimed.
question: Does oracle catalogue expansion remove nuisance-background errors under the paired absolute-admission and relative-score rule, and how much change comes from scores versus recalibration?
design: Full 2x2 crossing of scoring catalogue {canonical, expanded} and calibration catalogue {canonical, expanded}; regimes shifted, nuisance, outside; alpha 1/10 and 1/20. All 24 arms reported. Outside uses shifted calibration and has no in-catalogue true allele.
calibration: 128 calibration locus blocks, 12 reads per regime. Absolute score maximum is the maximum true-allele distance in each block. Relative score maximum is max(d_true - min(d_0,d_1)). Each gate uses alpha/2: order rank ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha/2)); infinity if rank>n. Thresholds saved before test decisions.
rule: Admit iff min(d_0,d_1)<=qA. Return allele a iff admitted and d_a-min(d_0,d_1)<=qR.
primary: Paired nuisance-regime comparison canonical/canonical versus expanded/expanded at alpha 1/20; report whole-block coverage, correct and wrong singletons, ambiguity, empty sets and each adverse record's transition. Do not select favourable alpha or geometry.
secondary: Crossed catalogue arms separate score changes from threshold changes. Report all geometry strata and source labels. The expanded catalogue is an oracle containing constructed nuisance templates; it does not discover unknown haplotypes.
validation: Verify complete input archives and every MP31 manifest entry; reproduce all six MP32 canonical/canonical aggregate arms exactly; independently recompute calibration order statistics and recount decisions after download.
custody: Three CPU batches, one regime per batch. Each produces a resumable archive, transferred through CLI and persisted to private Drive before the next batch. Reused checkpoints must match exact protocol and script hashes.
limits: No nominal guarantee for transferred thresholds, outside records or arbitrary distribution shift. Distant outside controls do not establish rejection of homologous negatives. Source-base ancestry obstruction remains unchanged.
